newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower on corporate trouble woes.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower on corporate trouble woes.

text.p: Seoul stocks ended Saturday's half-day session lower on investor worries about more corporate financial problems, brokers said.
The composite stock index fell 8.64 points to 678.98.
Brokers said market talk, denied by the company, that Midopa Department Store faced a liquidity problem sparked fears of more corporate failures.

"Investors are suspecting Midopa was in serious financial situation, it has spent too much to defend a hostile takeover attempt," said Hwang Chang-joong of LG Securities. "The market will remain weak next week on the Midopa woes."
Midopa went limit down, losing 900 won to 11,000.

Midopa was the target of South Korea's first major hostile takeover bid by Shindongbang Corp in March. The raid on the retailer fizzled out after Sungwon Group, once regarded as a partner of Shingdongbang, agreed to sell all its 12.6 pct stake to Midopa and its parent Dainong Group.
Core blue chips remained solid on institutional support, brokers said.
Foreigners' favourite POSCO rose 1,200 won to 52,000 and SK Telecom gained 2,000 won to 395,000.
Despite Midopa, a Ssangyong Securities broker said he believed the market would show gradual gains next week after ending its consolidation.
"The 670 level will be supportive as investors believed the market has hit the bottom. The worst is over for the nation's economy," he said.
